source.title: The Conflict Between Logic and Memory: Learning Higher-Order Interactions in Shallow MLPs

record.file_problem: The supplied text is the full paper; no apparent truncation or garbling that prevents extraction.
record.tranche_reason: The study tests optimizer and training-condition effects on held-out performance in shallow networks using synthetic composite and strict-parity tasks. These are conceptually related to generalization but do not test the catalog’s random-label memorization and natural-label generalization claim.
record.gate_note: The paper reports its own results on optimizer comparisons, interventions, task stages, modes, strict-parity orders, and CIFAR-10. Cited findings from prior work and generator-only latent-prefix audits are not rows. Rows include only reported model outcomes; result rows for V1–V8 are not applicable because none of those versions’ named behaviors is tested.
record.test_reason: The CIFAR-10 experiments test V4 in two convolutional architectures: Adam has lower held-out accuracy than SGDM under fixed learning rates and a common training budget. The record incorrectly excludes these optimizer comparisons. The synthetic experiments measure other generalization behaviors.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: permitted adaptation to nuisance connections changes both shared stage-level failures and relative optimizer advantages. Strict parity shows optimizer-dependent finite-budget learning, while the mixed task establishes that removing designated interference does not always recover performance. These outcomes do not establish a particular internal mechanism.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses shallow ReLU networks, composite synthetic tasks, strict parity, nuisance-adaptation interventions, and CIFAR-10 optimizer comparisons. It does not reproduce any listed original experiment or measure random-label memorization/generalization.
record.method_sensitivity: Results vary with task structure, optimizer, training constraint, strict-parity order, learning-rate and checkpoint selection, and convolutional architecture. In the rare-mode task, freezing background connections changes the optimizer gap; in the mixed task, removing non-target inputs does not recover stage 4. Strict-parity performance depends on order and the tested learning-rate grids and finite budget.

fits_no_version.finding: Freezing nuisance-connected weights raises hardest-stage accuracy to approximately 68–71%, whereas test-only masking leaves it near chance.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Restricting adaptation to known nuisance inputs can improve stage-specific generalization in shallow synthetic networks.

fits_no_version.finding: Cue removal improves vote-task accuracy, and cue dependence differs between vote and pairwise-mode tasks.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Optimizer cue reliance depends on task structure and competing evidence.

fits_no_version.finding: Background freezing improves rare-mode accuracy and reduces Muon's advantage over SGDM by 12.48 percentage points.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Optimizer subgroup advantages can depend on which nuisance connections remain trainable.

fits_no_version.finding: Removing all designated non-target inputs leaves mixed-task fourth-stage accuracy near chance.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Removing known interference does not ensure difficult-stage generalization.

fits_no_version.finding: Strict-parity accuracy separates across optimizers at intermediate orders and approaches chance at orders 13–20 despite a high Bayes reference.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Finite-budget learning of noisy strict parity can fail despite substantial predictive information; similar online training accuracy need not imply similar test accuracy.

fits_no_version.finding: Muon performance and the direction of classifier-head replacement effects differ between the two convolutional architectures.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The effect of spectral matrix updates and classifier-head update choices can depend on convolutional architecture.

record.problems: Three-seed synthetic summaries report sample standard deviations but no significance tests. Strict-parity Muon selected the lowest tested learning rate across orders 7–12, leaving lower rates untested; the authors also note late order-eleven SGDM checkpoints and finite-budget limitations. CIFAR-10 results use one seed and fixed learning rates. Freezing changes the number and location of trainable parameters, and the paper calls for matched-parameter-count controls. The twenty-configuration extension lacks stage-specific trajectories for all methods.
record.rows_left_out: The paper reports many additional optimizer-by-task aggregate and cue results, but only results bearing on the paper’s central generalization patterns were retained; the full expanded optimizer matrix in Appendix C.4 and additional condition-specific values in Tables 3, 6, 7, 9, 11, 14, and 15 are not cataloged exhaustively. No claim versions were tested, so no rows were required for V1–V8.

untested.parts: Random-label memorization and the paired natural-label versus random-label held-out comparison.
Width sweeps beyond zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.

Learning-rate and schedule searches, broader tuning, language benchmarks, matched training performance, decoupled-weight-decay recovery and switching from Adam to SGD. CIFAR-10 uses fixed learning rates.
Dropout interventions and removal with weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness, generalization-gap correlations and comparison with norm or margin measures.
Removing memorized training examples versus equally many random examples and retraining.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source for V4. The CIFAR-10 comparisons provide narrow supporting evidence, without demonstrating that the gaps survive learning-rate tuning. Additional Table 11 configurations are explicitly covered by rows_left_out, so they are not flagged as undeclared missing results.

versions.untested_parts: No random-label fitting or natural-label versus random-label held-out comparison.
No width sweep beyond the interpolation threshold.
No convolutional-versus-fully-connected comparison on images; CIFAR-10 results compare optimizer configurations within convolutional architectures.
Optimizer comparisons do not evaluate the stated adaptive-versus-SGD generalization claim on image or language benchmarks under its tuning conditions.
No batch-size comparison or large-batch training experiment.
No magnitude-aware sharpness measurement or comparison with norm- and margin-based measures.
No removal of memorized examples or retraining comparison.
